Work queue for controllers

Source: R/workqueue.R
WorkQueue.Rd

Work queue for controllers

Work queue for controllers

Details

A queue of object keys ("namespace/name") with the semantics of client-go's rate-limited work queue, which is what controllers use between their informers and their reconcile function:

  • A key is queued at most once. Ten events for one object before it is handled still mean one reconcile.

  • A key is never handed out twice at the same time. If it is added again while being processed, it goes back on the queue when done() is called, so the change is not lost.

  • add_after() makes a key available after a delay (for "check again in a minute"). If a key is delayed twice, the earlier time wins.

  • add_rate_limited() re-adds a key after a per-key exponential backoff (base_delay, doubling up to max_delay); forget() resets it after a success.

The usual loop is key <- q$get(), reconcile, then q$forget(key) on success or q$add_rate_limited(key) on failure, and finally q$done(key).

Method new()

Create a queue.

Usage

WorkQueue$new(
  base_delay = 0.005,
  max_delay = 1000,
  clock = function() as.numeric(Sys.time())
)

Arguments

base_delay

First retry delay for add_rate_limited(), seconds.

max_delay

Upper bound on the retry delay, seconds.

clock

Function returning the current time in seconds. Only for tests.

key

Delay in seconds; <= 0 adds now.

Take the next key to process, or NULL if none is ready. The caller must call done() with it afterwards.

Examples

q <- WorkQueue$new()
q$add("default/web"); q$add("default/web")
q$len()              # 1
#> [1] 1
key <- q$get()
q$add_rate_limited(key)   # failed: retry after base_delay
q$done(key)
q$next_ready_in()
#> [1] 0.004421473
